bootstrap.aws: Run cd deploy/aws/bootstrap && terraform init && terraform apply with your AWS sign-in. It creates state storage, an image registry, and one GitHub OIDC role per environment.
bootstrap.azure: Run cd deploy/azure/bootstrap && terraform init && terraform apply -var subscription_id=<id> with your Azure sign-in. It creates state storage, an image registry, and an Entra app with a federated credential per environment.
bootstrap.gcp: Run cd deploy/gcp/bootstrap && terraform init && terraform apply -var project_id=<id> with your Google Cloud sign-in. It creates state storage, an image registry, and a service account with Workload Identity Federation per environment.

setup.unzip: Unzip the backend and copy its example settings with cp .env.example .env.
setup.fillEnv: Fill in the variables below in .env using your own credentials.
setup.start: Start it with docker compose up --build, then open http://localhost:8000/docs.
setup.test: Run the tests with make test.
setup.smtpUser: Login for {{host}}:{{port}} from your email provider.
setup.smtpPassword: Password or API key for that login.
setup.keycloakUrlOwn: Use http://localhost:8081 locally and your HTTPS address in production.
setup.keycloakUrlExternal: The public address of your existing Keycloak.
setup.apiUrl: The public address of the API for sign-in callbacks. Use http://localhost:8000 locally.
setup.keycloakDb: A long random password for Keycloak’s database.
setup.keycloakAdmin: The first Keycloak admin account. Replace it with your own admin after signing in.
setup.keycloakIdp: The client secret from the provider console for {{name}}.
setup.keycloakExistingAdmin: An existing admin for the one-time registration script.
setup.keycloakRegister: Register this project with python scripts/keycloak_register.py to add clients and roles. The command can be run again.
setup.keycloakUsers: Create users in realm {{realm}}, assign their roles on client {{client}}, then choose Authorize in the API docs to sign in.
setup.keycloakOwn: Open the Keycloak admin console at http://localhost:8081/admin. Create your own admin account and remove the bootstrap admin.
setup.keycloakTenants: Create organizations and add each user to one. Each organization is a tenant.
setup.rsaKey: Generate the signing key with docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/srv -w /srv python:3.12-slim sh -c "pip install -q cryptography && python -m app.auth.keys".
setup.jwtSecret: Generate a signing secret of at least 32 characters with python3 -m app.auth.keys.
setup.twilio: Find the credential in your Twilio console.
setup.vonage: Find the credential in your Vonage dashboard.
setup.snsRegion: The AWS region SNS sends from.
setup.snsAccess: The AWS IAM credentials. An instance role can also provide access.
setup.redis: The refresh-token store. Compose supplies the URL locally.
setup.authRate: See app/auth/config.py for the generated rate limits. Limits count per worker.
setup.stripeKey: Use a test API key locally. A live key requires APP_ENV=production.
setup.stripeWebhook: Get the signing secret from Stripe’s webhook settings. List two comma-separated secrets during rotation.
setup.razorpayId: Find the key ID in Razorpay’s API key settings. Use a test key locally.
setup.razorpayKey: Save the matching secret when you create the key.
setup.razorpayWebhook: Use a secret of at least 16 characters. List two comma-separated secrets during rotation.
setup.paymentsWorker: Compose starts payments-worker alongside the API. See deploy/DEPLOYMENT.md for sizing and worker operation.
setup.storageUser: Set a long login for your S3-compatible server and local development store.
setup.storagePassword: Set a long random password for the storage login.
setup.storageEndpoint: The S3-compatible endpoint. Compose uses http://objectstore:8333 locally. Use HTTPS in production.
setup.storageIam: For AWS, give the service an IAM role with deploy/storage/iam-policy.json and leave these credentials blank.
setup.storageEnvironment: Set APP_ENV=production to enforce production storage requirements.
setup.storageLocal: Compose starts a local S3-compatible store. Set STORAGE_ENDPOINT_URL to your own server for production.
setup.storageBucket: Create the private bucket {{bucket}} using the commands in deploy/storage/STORAGE.md.
setup.storageStart: Start with docker compose up --build. Compose starts the ClamAV malware scanner.
setup.storageMaintenance: Run make storage-maintenance hourly and run it with --rescan daily.
setup.storageDocs: See deploy/storage/STORAGE.md and docs/storage-security.md for setup, operations, and erasure requests.

ship.eligibleBumps: Eligible. Every block change is a patch bump, the scorecard passes and no migration is involved.
ship.eligibleFiles: Eligible. Only generated files change, the scorecard passes and no migration is involved.
ship.eligibilityMigration: Review required. The proposal adds or changes a database migration.
ship.eligibilityScore: Review required. The scorecard has a failing check.
ship.eligibilityMajor: Review required. A block changes by a major version.
ship.eligibilityBump: Review required. A block changes by more than a patch version.
ship.eligibilityZone: Review required. Files outside the generated zone change.
ship.eligibilityOther: Review required. The proposal contains more than a patch-level change.
ship.eligibilityNote: This flag is informational. Apply the patch yourself before marking it applied.
